Text.style: background-color: white; padding: 10px; border-radius: 5px; border-left: 4px solid #2c5aa0; white-space: pre-wrap;

Choice.value: 1 - Biologically impossible (e.g., patient is both 30 and 73 years old)
2 - Highly implausible physiologically (e.g., lab values swing drastically without explanation)
3 - Possible but doubtful (e.g., stent documented as placed vs not placed)
4 - Possible and consistent with common clinical evolution (e.g., stable pneumothorax later worsens)
5 - Very realistic and frequent in practice (e.g., drug prescribed then later listed as allergy)
3 - Possible as noise or one-off error
4 - Common as EHR inconsistency (copy-paste, unsynchronized notes)
5 - Very common and typical of EHRs (e.g., allergy vs medication, past history vs acute event)
A - Hard contradiction: strong, medically meaningful inconsistency (allergy vs prescription, incompatible ages)
B - Apparent contradiction: actually normal clinical evolution but looks contradictory (stable vs worsened, no HTN vs new-onset HTN). Useful for testing false positives
C - Weak/noise: trivial inconsistency or artifact (e.g., de-identification error)
